title: Numerical abnormality — missing sex chromosome
clinical_history: A 14-year-old girl is referred for short stature and delayed puberty. Examination notes a low posterior hairline and a history of coarctation of the aorta repaired in infancy. Constitutional karyotyping is requested.
unknown_prompt: An adolescent with short stature and delayed puberty is referred for constitutional chromosome analysis. Construct the karyotype and provide the ISCN and most closely associated condition.
plain_language_interpretation: A karyotype with 45 chromosomes and a single X chromosome (monosomy X). ISCN does not use the obsolete token XO.
explanation: The ISCN for non-mosaic monosomy X is 45,X. Do not write 45,XO; the letter O is not used. Only one sex chromosome is present, so the count is 45. This constitutional finding is associated with Turner syndrome (short stature, ovarian dysgenesis, and increased risk of left-sided cardiac anomalies such as coarctation). Many clinical patients are mosaic (for example 45,X/46,XX), which is written with a slash between cell lines; this teaching case is the non-mosaic 45,X line.
hints: Count the chromosomes. A missing chromosome produces a count of 45 rather than 46.
Inspect the sex-chromosome slots. There is a single X and no Y.
ISCN writes a single X as 45,X. Do not add the letter O.
